title: Ticket triage → resolution or escalation
description: Classify inbound tickets, filter and rank them by measured impact, cut a queue that fits the shift, and route the top band to a named escalation owner.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-cs-01
  title: Ticket triage → resolution or escalation
  description: Classify inbound tickets, filter and rank them by measured impact, cut a queue that fits
    the shift, and route the top band to a named escalation owner.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Convert an undifferentiated inbound queue into ranked, capacity-sized work with an explicit
    escalation path and a verified resolution on every closed item.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: Inbound ticket batch
      summary: Inbound ticket batch
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The requester's objective, source material, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - tickets
              - entitlement_tier
              - known_incidents
              - shift_capacity
            properties:
              tickets: {}
              entitlement_tier: {}
              known_incidents: {}
              shift_capacity: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n-classify
      kind: agent
      templateRef: cs-01
      name: Classify by cause class and measured impact
      summary: Score and label every incoming item before anything is queued.
      role: Support triager classifying tickets by cause class, severity, and required expertise.
      prompt: You are a Support Triage Classifier. You classify each ticket by likely cause class, customer
        impact, and the expertise required to resolve it, and you return a confidence with every label
        so low-confidence routing can be reviewed rather than trusted. You separate a customer's stated
        urgency from measured impact and report both, because triaging on tone alone starves quiet outages
        of attention.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - evaluation
          - optimization
          - risk-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - search
        connectors:
          - mcp:helpdesk
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - label
          - severity
          - confidence
          - rationale
        properties:
          label: {}
          severity: {}
          confidence: {}
          rationale: {}
    - id: n-filter
      kind: transform
      name: Drop out-of-scope items
      summary: keep tickets that are in scope for this queue and not already attached to a known incident
      config:
        operation: filter
        expression: keep tickets that are in scope for this queue and not already attached to a known
          incident
    - id: n-rank
      kind: transform
      name: Rank by urgency
      summary: sort by measured_impact descending, then by sla_time_remaining ascending
      config:
        operation: sort
        expression: sort by measured_impact descending, then by sla_time_remaining ascending
    - id: n-queue
      kind: transform
      name: Cut the actionable queue
      summary: take the first shift_capacity tickets as this shift's queue
      config:
        operation: slice
        expression: take the first shift_capacity tickets as this shift's queue
    - id: n-severity
      kind: condition
      name: Severity routing
      summary: Route on ticket.severity selects one declared branch.
      config:
        expression: ticket.severity selects one declared branch
        branches:
          - label: Escalate
            when: escalate
          - label: Standard
            when: standard
          - label: Default
            when: default
    - id: n-escalate
      kind: agent
      templateRef: cs-03
      name: Own the escalated case to closure
      summary: Escalation path for the top band.
      role: Escalation owner running high-impact incidents through to customer closure.
      prompt: 'You are an Escalation Manager. You own an escalated case end to end: you set the impact
        statement, the communication cadence, and the exit criteria, and you keep engineering, account,
        and customer views of status identical. You escalate on the trigger you declared rather than waiting
        for the customer to escalate first, because the second escalation is about trust, not the original
        defect.'
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - communication
          - incident-response
        tools:
          - read
          - write
        connectors:
          - mcp:helpdesk
          - mcp:slack
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-handle
      kind: agent
      templateRef: cs-02
      name: Reproduce, diagnose, and verify the fix
      summary: Standard resolution path.
      role: Support engineer producing reproducible diagnoses and verified resolutions.
      prompt: You are a Resolution Specialist. You reproduce the reported behavior against the customer's
        actual configuration, state the diagnosis with the evidence that supports it, and give the customer
        a resolution plus the verification step that proves it worked. You say explicitly when you could
        not reproduce the issue instead of shipping a plausible fix, because an unverified fix returns
        as a worse ticket.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - product-management
          - clinical-review
          - evaluation
          - communication
          - risk-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - test
        connectors:
          - mcp:helpdesk
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-rejoin
      kind: join
      name: Reconverge after routing
      summary: Release whichever routed path completed.
      config:
        join: first
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: Support lead approves customer-facing escalation commitments
      summary: Pause for the support lead; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Ticket triage → resolution or escalation deliverable, the evidence
        behind it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-classify
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-2
      from: n-classify
      to: n-filter
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-3
      from: n-filter
      to: n-rank
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-4
      from: n-rank
      to: n-queue
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-5
      from: n-queue
      to: n-severity
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-6
      from: n-severity
      to: n-escalate
      kind: control
      condition: escalate
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-7
      from: n-severity
      to: n-handle
      kind: control
      condition: standard
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-8
      from: n-escalate
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-9
      from: n-handle
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-10
      from: n-rejoin
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-cs-01-edge-11
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
